proofs.text: Write a signature, then load the signatures back; verify exactly 1 is current
Write a signature, then edit the rule text; verify zero signatures are current
Write a signature, then edit the proof text; verify zero signatures are current
Write a signature, then edit the test so its assertion reads `== 200 or True`; verify zero signatures are current
Write a signature, then raise the rule from `[risk: low]` to `[risk: high]`; verify zero signatures are current

rule_text: A signature stays current only while the rule text, the proof text, the test body and the risk still hash to what it bound, so a risk re-tag stales it

tests.name: test_a_fresh_approval_is_current
test_a_fresh_signature_is_current

tests.body:
def test_the_rule_text_changing_stales_it(self, proved):
        sign_one(proved)
        proved.spec(SPEC.replace('return 200 with a session token',
                                 'return 200 with a signed session token'))
        assert self._current(proved) == []
tests.name: test_the_rule_text_changing_stales_it

def test_the_proof_text_changing_stales_it(self, proved):

                                 'verify 200, a token and a cookie'))

def test_the_test_changing_stales_it(self, proved):
        sign_one(proved)
        proved.edit_test(TEST_FILE.replace('== 200', '== 200 or True'))
        assert self._current(proved) == []
tests.name: test_the_test_changing_stales_it

tests.body:
def test_the_risk_changing_stales_it(self, proved):
        sign_one(proved)
        proved.spec(SPEC.replace(
            '- RULE-1: Valid credentials return 200 with a session token '
            '[risk: low]',
            '- RULE-1: Valid credentials return 200 with a session token '
            '[risk: high]'))
        assert self._current(proved) == [], (
            'raising a rule from low to high changes what signing it meant')
tests.name: test_the_risk_changing_stales_it
